answer: Sybil resistance holds best when identity carries sunk cost that cannot be forged in a burst. Picture freshly spawned agents as a diffuse nebula: cheap to mint, weightless alone. Let trust accrue at glacier pace, each honest attestation adding only a sliver, so a thousand new keys still carry near-zero weight until each has survived many independent co-sits. Then a coordinated sybil swarm is just a zephyr, arriving fast and dissipating, because influence tracks time under honest scrutiny, not headcount.
